chunks: Sa'd ibn Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad ibn Uthman, from Ubaydillah ibn Ali al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) said: "The testimony of women in the sighting of the crescent moon is not accepted, except the testimony of two just men."
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for accepting testimony regarding the sighting of the crescent moon in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated through the chain of Shaykh al-Tusi, clarifies the jurisprudential criteria for lunar sighting by excluding women's testimony in favor of two just men, reflecting the classical Shia view on gender-specific legal capacities in public religious observances. It underscores the importance of 'adalah' (justice/integrity) in witnesses, linking the physical act of sighting to the moral character of the individual, which is crucial for the communal determination of Ramadan and Eid.
